vulnerability.category_l2: Regular-expression denial of service (catastrophic backtracking) in Parser::cleanup()

critical_operation.description: Parser::cleanup() strips the optional %YAML directive header with #^\%YAML[: ][\d\.]+.*\n#u. The class [\d\.]+ and the following .* can both consume the same dots, so a crafted header made of many digits and dots drives catastrophic backtracking; the leading-comment regex at line 1014 has a nested quantifier; the document-start regex at line 1022 and the document-end regex at line 1029 are single-quantifier patterns that the advisory also hardens, but on their own they are not classically catastrophic. cleanup() runs at the start of parse(), before tokenization, so any untrusted YAML document reaches it and parsing can be made to hang for an arbitrarily long time. The 5.4.52 fix rewrites all four regexes with possessive quantifiers and unambiguous character classes.

entry_point.description: Yaml::parse() or Parser::parse() on untrusted YAML whose first line is an oversized %YAML directive (or an oversized leading comment or document marker).

trace.description: parse() calls cleanup() before tokenizing the document
the %YAML header regex with overlapping quantifiers runs on the crafted first line
the leading-comment regex uses a nested quantifier over lines

limitations: Single-reviewer dossier; not eligible for data/vulnerabilities.jsonl yet.
No PHP, regex engine or YAML document was executed; the backtracking blow-up was not timed.
Only the 5.4 branch was compared; 6.4.40, 7.4.12 and 8.0.12 were not diffed.
The 5.4 Parser.php at this tag predates the recursion-depth and alias-bounding commits (914f427e, e77391b2), so the fix diff is stacked on top of them.
The GHSA label LOW and OSV VA:L vector disagree materially with the CNA 8.7 and NVD 7.5 scores.

Independent review corrected a detail: the document-start regex is at line 1022, not 1024 (1024 is the offset comment); the %YAML, leading-comment and document-end line numbers (1010, 1014, 1029) were confirmed.
open_questions: Which of the four regexes is reachable first in a normal parse was not traced beyond reading the code.
Whether the document-end marker regex alone can be triggered without a preceding document-start marker was not analysed.
